en.title: An Angel Visits Mary
story: Now our trail goes back in time, to see how Jesus’ adventure on earth began.

In a little town called Nazareth lived a young woman named Mary. She was going to marry a carpenter named Joseph. She was not rich or famous. But one day an angel named Gabriel appeared to her! ‘Greetings! The Lord is with you,’ he said.

Mary was scared. ‘Don’t be afraid, Mary,’ said Gabriel. ‘God is pleased with you. You are going to have a baby boy, and you will call him Jesus. He will be the Son of God, and his kingdom will never end!’

‘How can this happen?’ Mary asked. ‘The Holy Spirit will make it happen,’ said the angel. ‘Nothing is impossible with God.’ And Mary said, ‘I am the Lord’s servant. Let it happen just as you said.’ Mary said YES to God.

en.title: The Word Became Flesh
story: Christmas begins long before Bethlehem. John’s Gospel starts at the very beginning: ‘In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God… Through Him all things were made.’ The ‘Word’ is the eternal Son of God, the One who spoke creation into being in Genesis 1. Then comes one of the most astonishing sentences ever written: ‘The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us.’

The theological word for this is incarnation: God taking on a human body. Jesus didn’t stop being God when He became human. He was fully God and fully human, one person. The Creator of galaxies became an embryo.

Luke shows us how it happened. The angel Gabriel visited a young woman named Mary in Nazareth, an unimportant village. ‘You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call Him Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High… His kingdom will never end.’

Mary asked an honest question: ‘How will this be, since I am a virgin?’ Gabriel explained: ‘The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God.’ Then: ‘No word from God will ever fail.’

Mary was probably a teenager. Saying yes could cost her reputation, her engagement, even her safety. Yet she answered, ‘I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled.’ Her faith wasn’t the absence of questions. It was trust in God’s character in spite of them.

Why does the incarnation matter? Because it means God doesn’t love us from a distance. He came close enough to be touched, to feel tired, hungry, sad and tempted. The book of Hebrews says that because of this, we have a High Priest who can sympathise with our weaknesses. When you pray, you are talking to Someone who knows what it is like to be human.

verse.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us.

lessons: Jesus is the eternal Word, fully God and fully human: the incarnation.
God came close to us in Jesus; He understands what it is to be human.
Mary shows us faith that asks honest questions and still says yes to God.

Why does it matter that Jesus was fully human as well as fully God?

af.title: Die Woord het Mens Geword
story: Kersfees begin lank voor Betlehem. Johannes se Evangelie begin by die heel begin: ‘In die begin was die Woord, en die Woord was by God, en die Woord was God… Alles het deur Hom ontstaan.’ Die ‘Woord’ is die ewige Seun van God, die Een wat die skepping in Genesis 1 laat ontstaan het. Dan kom een van die verbasendste sinne wat nog ooit geskryf is: ‘Die Woord het mens geword en het onder ons kom woon.’

Die teologiese woord hiervoor is vleeswording: God wat ’n menslike liggaam aanneem. Jesus het nie opgehou om God te wees toe Hy mens geword het nie. Hy was ten volle God en ten volle mens, een persoon. Die Skepper van sterrestelsels het ’n embrio geword.

Lukas wys ons hoe dit gebeur het. Die engel Gabriël het ’n jong vrou met die naam Maria in Nasaret besoek, ’n onbelangrike dorpie. ‘Jy sal swanger word en ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem. Hy sal groot wees en die Seun van die Allerhoogste genoem word… Aan sy koningskap sal daar geen einde wees nie.’

Maria het ’n eerlike vraag gevra: ‘Hoe sal dit gebeur, want ek is nog ’n maagd?’ Gabriël het verduidelik: ‘Die Heilige Gees sal oor jou kom, en die krag van die Allerhoogste sal jou oorskadu. Daarom sal die heilige kind wat gebore word, die Seun van God genoem word.’ Toe: ‘Geen woord van God sal ooit misluk nie.’

Maria was seker ’n tiener. Om ja te sê kon haar reputasie, haar verlowing, selfs haar veiligheid kos. Tog het sy geantwoord: ‘Ek is die dienares van die Here. Laat dit met my gebeur soos u gesê het.’ Haar geloof was nie die afwesigheid van vrae nie. Dit was vertroue in God se karakter ten spyte daarvan.

Hoekom maak die vleeswording saak? Omdat dit beteken God het ons nie van ver af lief nie. Hy het naby genoeg gekom om aangeraak te word, om moeg, honger, hartseer en versoek te voel. Die boek Hebreërs sê dat ons daarom ’n Hoëpriester het wat met ons swakhede kan meevoel. As jy bid, praat jy met Iemand wat weet hoe dit is om mens te wees.

verse.text: Die Woord het mens geword en het onder ons kom woon.

lessons: Jesus is die ewige Woord, ten volle God en ten volle mens: die vleeswording.

en.title: Mary’s Yes
story: Our Christmas trail begins in Nazareth, a small village in the hills of Galilee that nobody thought was important. There lived a young woman named Mary. She was engaged to a carpenter called Joseph, a descendant of King David.
One day God sent the angel Gabriel to her. ‘Greetings, you who are highly favoured! The Lord is with you.’ Mary was deeply troubled. What could this mean?

‘Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favour with God,’ the angel said. ‘You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call Him Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David… His kingdom will never end.’ Remember Isaiah’s clues? This was the promised King!

Mary asked an honest question: ‘How will this be, since I am a virgin?’ The angel explained that the Holy Spirit would come upon her, and ‘the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God’. Jesus would be fully human, born of Mary, and fully God, the Son of God. Gabriel added that Mary’s elderly relative Elizabeth, who had never been able to have children, was expecting a baby too. ‘For no word from God will ever fail.’

Mary didn’t understand everything. Saying yes could bring her shame and danger, because people might not believe her story. But she answered with beautiful trust: ‘I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled.’

God chose an ordinary young woman from a forgotten village for the most important job in history. He still chooses ordinary people. And He still looks for hearts that say, ‘Yes, Lord. Let it be as you say.’

verse.text: I am the Lord’s servant. May your word to me be fulfilled.

lessons: Jesus is the promised King, fully God and fully human.
God chooses ordinary people for His great plans.
Saying yes to God means trusting Him even when we don’t understand everything.

Why might it have been hard for Mary to say yes?

af.title: Maria se Ja
story: Ons Kerspad begin in Nasaret, ’n klein dorpie in die heuwels van Galilea wat niemand as belangrik gesien het nie. Daar het ’n jong vrou met die naam Maria gewoon. Sy was verloof aan ’n timmerman met die naam Josef, ’n afstammeling van koning Dawid.
Eendag het God die engel Gabriël na haar gestuur. ‘Wees gegroet, jy wat begenadig is! Die Here is met jou.’ Maria was baie ontsteld. Wat kon dit beteken?

‘Moenie bang wees nie, Maria; God is baie goed vir jou,’ het die engel gesê. ‘Jy sal swanger word en ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem. Hy sal groot wees en die Seun van die Allerhoogste genoem word. Die Here God sal Hom die troon van sy vader Dawid gee… Aan sy koningskap sal daar geen einde wees nie.’ Onthou jy Jesaja se leidrade? Dit was die beloofde Koning!

Maria het ’n eerlike vraag gevra: ‘Hoe sal dit gebeur, want ek is nog ’n maagd?’ Die engel het verduidelik dat die Heilige Gees oor haar sou kom, en ‘die heilige kind wat gebore word, sal die Seun van God genoem word’. Jesus sou heeltemal mens wees, gebore uit Maria, en heeltemal God, die Seun van God. Gabriël het bygevoeg dat Maria se bejaarde familielid Elisabet, wat nooit kinders kon kry nie, ook ’n baba verwag. ‘Want geen woord van God sal ooit misluk nie.’

Maria het nie alles verstaan nie. Om ja te sê kon vir haar skande en gevaar bring, want mense sou dalk nie haar storie glo nie. Maar sy het met pragtige vertroue geantwoord: ‘Ek is die dienares van die Here. Laat dit met my gebeur soos u gesê het.’

God het ’n gewone jong vrou uit ’n vergete dorpie gekies vir die belangrikste werk in die geskiedenis. Hy kies vandag nog gewone mense. En Hy soek steeds harte wat sê: ‘Ja, Here. Laat dit wees soos U sê.’

verse.text: Ek is die dienares van die Here. Laat dit met my gebeur soos u gesê het.

lessons: Jesus is die beloofde Koning, heeltemal God en heeltemal mens.
God kies gewone mense vir sy groot planne.

en.title: Joseph's Dream
story: When Joseph heard that Mary was going to have a baby, he was confused and worried. What should he do?

One night, while Joseph was sleeping, an angel appeared to him in a dream. ‘Joseph, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The baby inside her is from the Holy Spirit. She will have a son, and you are to name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.’
Remember Isaiah’s clue? The angel said this was exactly what God had promised: ‘They will call him Immanuel,’ which means ‘God with us.’

When Joseph woke up, he did exactly what the angel said. He married Mary and got ready to look after God’s Son. God was coming to be with his people: not far away up in the sky, but right here, as one of us!

The name Jesus means ‘God saves’.
Joseph obeyed God straight away.

en.title: The Quiet Obedience of Joseph
story: Joseph is easy to overlook in the Christmas story. He has no lines. Not a single word he spoke is recorded in the Bible. Yet his quiet faithfulness made him the earthly father who raised the Son of God.

Imagine Joseph’s position. He was engaged to Mary, and engagement then was as binding as marriage. Then he discovered she was pregnant, and he knew the child wasn’t his. Every natural feeling would have been hurt and betrayal. The law allowed him to expose her publicly.

But Matthew tells us Joseph was ‘faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace’, so he planned to divorce her quietly. Even when he believed he had been wronged, he chose mercy over revenge. That tells you a lot about his heart.

Then an angel appeared to him in a dream: ‘Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.’

The name Jesus, Yeshua in Hebrew, means ‘the Lord saves’. Matthew connects it to Isaiah’s promise: ‘They will call Him Immanuel’, which means ‘God with us’. These two names sum up Christmas: God came to be with us, and He came to save us.

Then comes the sentence that defines Joseph: ‘When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him.’ No argument. No delay. He took Mary home, endured the gossip of a small town, protected her, and named the baby Jesus.

Joseph shows us that faith often looks less like dramatic speeches and more like quiet, immediate obedience when no one is applauding. God sees that kind of faithfulness, and He entrusts great things to people who are faithful in it.

verse.text: She will give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.

lessons: Jesus’ names tell us why He came: God with us (Immanuel) and the Lord saves (Jesus).
Joseph chose mercy even when he thought he had been wronged.

af.title: Die Stil Gehoorsaamheid van Josef
story: Josef word maklik in die Kersverhaal oor die hoof gesien. Hy het geen woorde nie. Nie een woord wat hy gesê het, word in die Bybel opgeteken nie. Tog het sy stil getrouheid hom die aardse pa gemaak wat die Seun van God grootgemaak het.

Stel jou Josef se posisie voor. Hy was verloof aan Maria, en ’n verlowing was toe so bindend soos ’n huwelik. Toe het hy uitgevind sy is swanger, en hy het geweet die kind is nie syne nie. Elke natuurlike gevoel sou seer en verraad gewees het. Die wet het hom toegelaat om haar in die openbaar aan die kaak te stel.

Maar Matteus vertel ons Josef was ‘regverdig, en wou haar nie in die openbaar in die skande steek nie’, toe beplan hy om stilletjies van haar te skei. Selfs toe hy geglo het hy is verontreg, het hy genade bo wraak gekies. Dit sê jou baie oor sy hart.

Toe verskyn ’n engel in ’n droom aan hom: ‘Josef, seun van Dawid, moenie bang wees om Maria as jou vrou huis toe te neem nie, want wat in haar verwek is, is van die Heilige Gees. Sy sal ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem, want Hy sal sy volk van hulle sondes red.’

Die naam Jesus, Jesua in Hebreeus, beteken ‘die Here red’. Matteus verbind dit met Jesaja se belofte: ‘Hulle sal Hom Immanuel noem’, wat beteken ‘God by ons’. Hierdie twee name som Kersfees op: God het gekom om by ons te wees, en Hy het gekom om ons te red.

Dan kom die sin wat Josef beskryf: ‘Toe Josef wakker word, het hy gedoen wat die engel van die Here hom beveel het.’ Geen argument nie. Geen uitstel nie. Hy het Maria huis toe geneem, die skinderpraatjies van ’n klein dorpie verduur, haar beskerm, en die baba Jesus genoem.

Josef wys ons dat geloof dikwels minder lyk soos dramatiese toesprake en meer soos stil, onmiddellike gehoorsaamheid wanneer niemand hande klap nie. God sien daardie soort getrouheid, en Hy vertrou groot dinge toe aan mense wat daarin getrou is.

verse.text: Sy sal ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem, want Hy sal sy volk van hulle sondes red.

lessons: Jesus se name sê vir ons hoekom Hy gekom het: God by ons (Immanuel) en die Here red (Jesus).
Josef het genade gekies selfs toe hy gedink het hy is verontreg.

prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U God by ons is en dat U red.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy genade gekies het (of kon gekies het) in plaas van om terug te kry. Wat het dit gekos? Wat het dit gewys?

en.title: Joseph’s Dream
story: Joseph was going to marry Mary.

In a dream, an angel said: ‘Joseph, Mary’s baby is God’s Son!’
‘Call Him Jesus. He will be called Immanuel: God with us!’
Joseph woke up and did what God said. God came to be with us!

verse.text: Immanuel means God with us.

en.action: Lie down and pretend to sleep: snore, snore! Then wake up, stretch, and say: ‘God is with us!’
lessons: God is with me.
questions: Where is God right now? (Here with us!)
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you are with me. Amen.

af.title: Josef se Droom
story: Josef sou met Maria trou.
Een nag het Josef vas geslaap. Snork, snork!
In ’n droom het ’n engel gesê: ‘Josef, Maria se baba is God se Seun!’
‘Noem Hom Jesus. Hy sal Immanuel genoem word: God by ons!’
Josef het wakker geword en gedoen wat God gesê het. God het gekom om by ons te wees!

af.action: Lê neer en maak of jy slaap: snork, snork! Word dan wakker, rek uit, en sê: ‘God is by ons!’
lessons: God is by my.

en.title: God With Us
story: Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth, engaged to Mary. In those days an engagement was almost as binding as marriage. Then Joseph discovered that Mary was expecting a baby, and he knew he wasn’t the father.

Imagine how Joseph felt: hurt, confused, perhaps betrayed. Matthew tells us Joseph was ‘faithful to the law, and yet did not want to expose her to public disgrace’. So he planned to break off the engagement quietly. Even in his pain, he chose kindness.

But while Joseph was thinking about this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream: ‘Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.’
Jesus is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Yeshua (Joshua), which means ‘the Lord saves’. His very name described His mission: to rescue us from sin.

Matthew explains that all this fulfilled Isaiah’s promise: ‘The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel’, which means ‘God with us’. This is the heart of Christmas. God didn’t just send a message or a helper from far away. God Himself came to be with us, as a real human baby.

‘When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him.’ He didn’t argue or delay. He married Mary, protected her, and when the baby was born he named Him Jesus. Joseph’s quiet, immediate obedience made him the earthly father who raised the Son of God.

verse.text: ‘The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel’ (which means ‘God with us’).

lessons: Jesus is Immanuel: God Himself came to be with us.
Jesus’ name means ‘the Lord saves’; He came to save us from our sins.
Joseph shows us quiet, immediate obedience and kindness, even when life is confusing.
questions: What did Joseph plan to do before the angel spoke to him? What does that show about him?
What does the name Jesus mean? What does Immanuel mean?
How does it help you to know that God is ‘with you’?
en.listen: Be still and remind yourself: ‘God is with me, right here.’ Ask Him: ‘Lord, where have you been with me today?’ Listen and remember.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you are Immanuel, God with us.
Thank you that you came to save me from my sin.
Help me to obey you quickly, like Joseph, when…

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you are asked to do something right, do it straight away, like Joseph, without arguing or delaying.

en.journal: Write ‘Immanuel: God with us’ at the top of a page. Draw or list all the places God is with you: at home, at school, at night, when you’re scared…

af.title: God by Ons
story: Josef was ’n timmerman in Nasaret, verloof aan Maria. In daardie dae was ’n verlowing amper so bindend soos ’n huwelik. Toe het Josef uitgevind dat Maria ’n baba verwag, en hy het geweet hy is nie die pa nie.

Stel jou voor hoe Josef gevoel het: seergemaak, deurmekaar, dalk verraai. Matteus vertel ons Josef was ‘’n regverdige man en wou haar nie in die openbaar in die skande steek nie’. Toe beplan hy om die verlowing stilletjies te verbreek. Selfs in sy pyn het hy gekies om goed te wees.

Maar terwyl Josef hieroor gedink het, het ’n engel van die Here in ’n droom aan hom verskyn: ‘Josef, seun van Dawid, moenie bang wees om Maria as jou vrou huis toe te neem nie, want wat in haar verwek is, is van die Heilige Gees. Sy sal ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem, want Hy sal sy volk van hulle sondes red.’
Jesus is die Griekse vorm van die Hebreeuse naam Jesua (Josua), wat beteken ‘die Here red’. Sy naam self het sy opdrag beskryf: om ons van sonde te red.

Matteus verduidelik dat dit alles Jesaja se belofte vervul het: ‘Die maagd sal swanger word en ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en hulle sal Hom Immanuel noem’, wat beteken ‘God by ons’. Dit is die hart van Kersfees. God het nie net ’n boodskap of ’n helper van ver af gestuur nie. God self het gekom om by ons te wees, as ’n regte mensebaba.

‘Toe Josef wakker word, het hy gedoen wat die engel van die Here hom beveel het.’ Hy het nie gestry of uitgestel nie. Hy het met Maria getrou, haar beskerm, en toe die baba gebore is, het hy Hom Jesus genoem. Josef se stil, onmiddellike gehoorsaamheid het hom die aardse pa gemaak wat die Seun van God grootgemaak het.

verse.text: ‘Die maagd sal swanger word en ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en hulle sal Hom Immanuel noem’ (dit beteken ‘God by ons’).

lessons: Jesus is Immanuel: God self het gekom om by ons te wees.
Jesus se naam beteken ‘die Here red’; Hy het gekom om ons van ons sondes te red.
Josef wys ons stil, onmiddellike gehoorsaamheid en goedheid, selfs as die lewe verwarrend is.
questions: Wat het Josef beplan om te doen voordat die engel met hom gepraat het? Wat wys dit oor hom?
Wat beteken die naam Jesus? Wat beteken Immanuel?
Hoe help dit jou om te weet dat God ‘by jou’ is?
af.listen: Wees stil en herinner jouself: ‘God is by my, hier.’ Vra Hom: ‘Here, waar was U vandag by my?’ Luister en onthou.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U Immanuel is, God by ons.
Dankie dat U gekom het om my van my sonde te red.
Help my om U vinnig te gehoorsaam, soos Josef, wanneer…

mission.text: As jy môre gevra word om iets regs te doen, doen dit dadelik, soos Josef, sonder om te stry of uit te stel.

af.journal: Skryf ‘Immanuel: God by ons’ bo-aan ’n bladsy. Teken of skryf al die plekke waar God by jou is: by die huis, by die skool, in die nag, as jy bang is…

en.title: The Long Trip to Bethlehem
story: The Roman emperor, Caesar Augustus, made a law: ‘Everyone must go to their family’s hometown to be counted!’ Joseph’s family came from Bethlehem, the town of King David.

So Joseph and Mary packed up and set off. It was a long, long trip, about as far as driving for two hours, but they had to walk! Over hills and dusty roads it went. Mary was about to have her baby. It took many days.

Why does this matter? Remember the clue from the prophet Micah, hundreds of years before? He said the Rescuer would be born in Bethlehem! Mary lived in Nazareth, far away. But God used an emperor’s law to bring Mary to exactly the right town at exactly the right time.
God takes care of every tiny detail. He is never late, and his promises always come true.

verse.text: But you, Bethlehem… out of you will come a ruler.

lessons: God is faithful. His promises come true right down to the details.
God is in charge, even of kings and emperors.
Long, hard journeys are easier when God is with us.
questions: What is the longest trip you have been on?
What little details of your life does God care about?
prayer: Dear God,
you take care of every little detail.
Thank you that your promises
always come true. Amen.

mission.text: Set out a nativity set (or draw one). Put Mary and Joseph far from the stable and move them a little closer each night.

af.title: Die Lang Reis na Betlehem
story: Die Romeinse keiser, Augustus, het ’n wet gemaak: ‘Almal moet na hulle familie se tuisdorp gaan om getel te word!’ Josef se familie het van Betlehem gekom, die dorp van koning Dawid.

Toe pak Josef en Maria op en vertrek. Dit was ’n lang, lang reis, omtrent so ver soos twee uur se ry met ’n motor, maar hulle moes loop! Oor heuwels en stowwerige paaie. Maria was amper gereed om haar baba te kry. Dit het baie dae gevat.

Hoekom is dit belangrik? Onthou die leidraad van die profeet Miga, honderde jare tevore? Hy het gesê die Redder sal in Betlehem gebore word! Maria het in Nasaret gewoon, ver weg. Maar God het ’n keiser se wet gebruik om Maria op presies die regte tyd na presies die regte dorp te bring.
God sorg vir elke klein detail. Hy is nooit laat nie, en sy beloftes word altyd waar.

verse.text: Maar jy, Betlehem… uit jou sal ’n heerser kom.

lessons: God is getrou. Sy beloftes word waar, tot in die kleinste detail.
God is in beheer, selfs oor konings en keisers.
Lang, moeilike reise is makliker as God by ons is.
questions: Wat is die langste reis wat jy al gemaak het?
Watter klein detailjies in jou lewe gee God om oor?
prayer: Liewe God,
U sorg vir elke klein detail.
Dankie dat u beloftes
altyd waar word. Amen.

en.title: Every Detail
story: About seven hundred years before Jesus was born, the prophet Micah wrote: ‘But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times.’ Notice two things: a specific little town, and a ruler whose origins are ‘from ancient times’, a hint that this King existed long before His birth.
Now fast forward. Mary and Joseph live in Nazareth, more than a hundred kilometres north of Bethlehem. Mary is heavily pregnant. There is no reason for them to be anywhere near Bethlehem.

Then the most powerful man in the world, Caesar Augustus, issues a decree for a census, probably for taxation. Everyone must register in their ancestral town. Because Joseph was descended from King David, he had to go to Bethlehem, David’s town. So a pagan emperor in Rome, pursuing his own interests and with no idea that the God of Israel existed in any way that mattered to him, moved a carpenter and his pregnant fiancée to exactly the right place at exactly the right time.

This is what the Bible means by God’s sovereignty: God is in charge of history. He works through kings and laws, timing and inconvenience, to fulfil His promises. Proverbs says, ‘In their hearts humans plan their course, but the Lord establishes their steps.’

From Mary and Joseph’s point of view, this probably felt like an unfair, badly timed government requirement: a week of hard travel at the worst possible moment. They couldn’t see the prophecy being fulfilled. They just had to be faithful in the inconvenience.

That is often how God’s guidance feels from the inside. Situations that seem random or frustrating may be God moving you into position. Christmas reminds us that God keeps His promises right down to the address. And if He was that precise about Bethlehem, you can trust Him with the details of your life.

verse.text: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel.

lessons: God keeps His promises down to the smallest detail, even across centuries.
God is sovereign: He works through rulers, laws and timing to fulfil His purposes.
Inconvenient or frustrating situations may be God moving us into position.
questions: Why do you think Micah’s prophecy mentions the ruler’s ‘origins from ancient times’?
How did God use Caesar’s decree? What does that show about who is really in charge?
What frustrating situation in your life might God be using?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Ask God: ‘Is there an inconvenience in my life that you are using for good?’ Write down what you sense.
prayer: God, you are sovereign over history and over my life.
I trust you with the details of…

af.title: Elke Detail
story: Omtrent sewehonderd jaar voor Jesus gebore is, het die profeet Miga geskryf: ‘Maar jy, Betlehem Efrata, al is jy klein onder die stamme van Juda, uit jou sal daar vir My een kom wat heerser oor Israel sal wees, wie se oorsprong van lank gelede is, van ou tye af.’ Let op twee dinge: ’n spesifieke klein dorpie, en ’n heerser wie se oorsprong ‘van ou tye af’ is, ’n wenk dat hierdie Koning lank voor sy geboorte bestaan het.
Spring nou vorentoe. Maria en Josef woon in Nasaret, meer as honderd kilometer noord van Betlehem. Maria is hoogswanger. Daar is geen rede vir hulle om enigsins naby Betlehem te wees nie.

Toe vaardig die magtigste man in die wêreld, keiser Augustus, ’n bevel uit vir ’n sensus, waarskynlik vir belasting. Almal moet in hulle voorvaderlike dorp registreer. Omdat Josef van koning Dawid afgestam het, moes hy na Betlehem gaan, Dawid se stad. So het ’n heidense keiser in Rome, wat sy eie belange nagejaag het en geen benul gehad het dat die God van Israel vir hom saak maak nie, ’n timmerman en sy swanger verloofde na presies die regte plek op presies die regte tyd geskuif.

Dit is wat die Bybel bedoel met God se soewereiniteit: God is in beheer van die geskiedenis. Hy werk deur konings en wette, tydsberekening en ongerief, om sy beloftes te vervul. Spreuke sê: ‘’n Mens beplan sy pad in sy hart, maar die Here bepaal sy treë.’

Uit Maria en Josef se oogpunt het dit seker gevoel soos ’n onregverdige, sleg getimede regeringsvereiste: ’n week se moeilike reis op die slegste moontlike oomblik. Hulle kon nie sien hoe die profesie vervul word nie. Hulle moes net getrou wees in die ongerief.

So voel God se leiding dikwels van binne af. Situasies wat lukraak of frustrerend lyk, kan God wees wat jou in posisie skuif. Kersfees herinner ons dat God sy beloftes tot by die adres hou. En as Hy so presies was oor Betlehem, kan jy Hom met die besonderhede van jou lewe vertrou.

verse.text: Maar jy, Betlehem Efrata, al is jy klein onder die stamme van Juda, uit jou sal daar vir My een kom wat heerser oor Israel sal wees.

lessons: God hou sy beloftes tot in die kleinste detail, selfs oor eeue heen.
God is soewerein: Hy werk deur heersers, wette en tydsberekening om sy doele te vervul.
Ongerieflike of frustrerende situasies kan God wees wat ons in posisie skuif.

Hoe het God die keiser se bevel gebruik? Wat wys dit oor wie regtig in beheer is?
Watter frustrerende situasie in jou lewe gebruik God dalk?

So Mary and Joseph went on a long, long trip to Bethlehem.

God was with them all the way!

en.title: Right on Time
story: Seven hundred years before Jesus was born, the prophet Micah wrote down a clue: ‘But you, Bethlehem… though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times.’
There was a problem, though. Mary and Joseph lived in Nazareth, more than a hundred kilometres away. And the baby was due very soon.

Then, far away in Rome, the most powerful man in the world made a decision. Caesar Augustus ordered a census: everyone in the empire had to register in their family’s home town, probably so they could be taxed. The emperor had no idea he was part of God’s plan.

Because Joseph was descended from King David, he had to go to Bethlehem, ‘the town of David’. So Joseph and Mary set off on the long journey south: about 145 kilometres over hills and dusty roads, perhaps a week of walking, with Mary heavily pregnant. It must have been exhausting and uncomfortable.

From the outside, it probably looked like bad timing and an unfair law. But God was arranging every detail. He used a pagan emperor’s decree to bring Mary and Joseph to exactly the right town at exactly the right time, so that His 700-year-old promise would come true.

God is faithful. He keeps His promises right down to the smallest detail, and He is never late. When your life feels like a long, uncomfortable journey, remember Bethlehem: God may be using things you don’t understand to bring you exactly where He wants you to be.

verse.text: But you, Bethlehem, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel.

lessons: God is faithful: He keeps His promises right down to the smallest detail.
God is in charge, even of emperors and their laws.
God can use hard, confusing journeys to bring us where He wants us to be.

af.title: Presies op Tyd
story: Sewehonderd jaar voordat Jesus gebore is, het die profeet Miga ’n leidraad neergeskryf: ‘Maar jy, Betlehem… al is jy klein onder die stamme van Juda, uit jou sal daar vir My een kom wat heerser oor Israel sal wees, wie se oorsprong van lank gelede is, van ou tye af.’
Daar was egter ’n probleem. Maria en Josef het in Nasaret gewoon, meer as honderd kilometer ver. En die baba sou baie gou gebore word.

Toe, ver weg in Rome, het die magtigste man in die wêreld ’n besluit geneem. Keiser Augustus het ’n sensus beveel: almal in die ryk moes in hulle familie se tuisdorp registreer, waarskynlik sodat hulle belasting kon betaal. Die keiser het geen idee gehad dat hy deel van God se plan was nie.

Omdat Josef van koning Dawid afgestam het, moes hy na Betlehem gaan, ‘die stad van Dawid’. Toe het Josef en Maria op die lang reis suid vertrek: omtrent 145 kilometer oor heuwels en stowwerige paaie, dalk ’n week se stap, met Maria hoogswanger. Dit moes uitputtend en ongemaklik gewees het.

Van buite af het dit seker gelyk soos slegte tydsberekening en ’n onregverdige wet. Maar God het elke detail gereël. Hy het ’n heidense keiser se bevel gebruik om Maria en Josef op presies die regte tyd na presies die regte dorp te bring, sodat sy 700 jaar oue belofte waar kon word.

God is getrou. Hy hou sy beloftes tot in die kleinste detail, en Hy is nooit laat nie. As jou lewe voel soos ’n lang, ongemaklike reis, onthou Betlehem: God gebruik dalk dinge wat jy nie verstaan nie om jou presies te bring waar Hy jou wil hê.

en.title: No Room!
story: When Mary and Joseph finally arrived in Bethlehem, the town was packed with people. Knock, knock. ‘Sorry, no room!’ Knock, knock. ‘Full up!’ There was nowhere to stay, and Mary’s baby was coming soon.

At last they found a place where animals were kept. It wasn’t a palace. It was probably smelly, with straw on the floor, a donkey and maybe some cows and sheep. And there, that very night, baby Jesus was born!
Mary wrapped him snugly in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, a feeding box for animals.

Think about this: Jesus is the King of the whole universe. He made the stars and the oceans! But he didn’t come with a crown and a castle. He came as a tiny baby in a stable. That is called being humble. Jesus came small so that everyone, rich or poor, could come close to him.

We can make room in our hearts for Jesus.

en.title: He Made Himself Nothing
story: Luke describes the birth of Jesus in remarkably few words: ‘While they were there, the time came for the baby to be born, and she gave birth to her firstborn, a son. She wrapped Him in cloths and placed Him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them.’
A manger is an animal feeding trough. The King of kings, through whom all things were made, spent His first night on earth in a place meant for animals.

Paul, writing to the church in Philippi, explains what this means. Jesus, ‘being in very nature God, did not consider equality with God something to be used to His own advantage; rather, He made Himself nothing by taking the very nature of a servant, being made in human likeness. And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself by becoming obedient to death, even death on a cross!’

Look at the direction of that passage: down, down, down. From heaven to earth. From God to servant. From life to death. From honour to the shame of a cross. The manger is the first step on that downward road, and the cross is the bottom.
Then the direction reverses: ‘Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place… that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.’ The way up in God’s kingdom is down.

Paul doesn’t write this just as theology. He writes it as a pattern for us: ‘In your relationships with one another, have the same mindset as Christ Jesus.’ Just before that: ‘Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.’

We live in a world that tells us to promote ourselves, build our image, get noticed, and be first. Christmas shows us a God who chose the opposite: He came low, served others and put their good above His own comfort. Humility isn’t thinking badly of yourself. It is thinking about yourself less, and about others more, because you are secure in God’s love.

verse.text: He made Himself nothing by taking the very nature of a servant, being made in human likeness.

lessons: Jesus, fully God, humbled Himself and was born in a manger.
The way up in God’s kingdom is down: humility and service.

af.title: Hy het Homself Ontledig
story: Lukas beskryf die geboorte van Jesus in merkwaardig min woorde: ‘Terwyl hulle daar was, het die tyd vir die baba aangebreek om gebore te word, en sy het haar eersteling, ’n seun, in die wêreld gebring. Sy het Hom in doeke toegedraai en in ’n krip neergelê, omdat daar vir hulle geen plek in die gastekamer was nie.’
’n Krip is ’n voerbak vir diere. Die Koning van die konings, deur wie alles ontstaan het, het sy eerste nag op aarde deurgebring op ’n plek wat vir diere bedoel was.

Paulus, wat aan die kerk in Filippi skryf, verduidelik wat dit beteken. Jesus, ‘al was Hy self God, het sy gelykheid aan God nie vir Homself gehou nie, maar Hom ontledig deur die gestalte van ’n dienskneg aan te neem en aan mense gelyk te word. En toe Hy as mens verskyn het, het Hy Homself verneder deur gehoorsaam te word tot die dood, ja, tot die dood aan die kruis!’

Kyk na die rigting van daardie gedeelte: af, af, af. Van die hemel na die aarde. Van God na dienskneg. Van lewe na dood. Van eer na die skande van ’n kruis. Die krip is die eerste tree op daardie pad na onder, en die kruis is die bodem.
Dan draai die rigting om: ‘Daarom het God Hom ook hoog verhef… sodat in die Naam van Jesus elke knie sal buig.’ Die pad na bo in God se koninkryk is na onder.

Paulus skryf dit nie net as teologie nie. Hy skryf dit as ’n patroon vir ons: ‘Julle moet in julle verhoudings met mekaar dieselfde gesindheid hê as Christus Jesus.’ Net voor dit: ‘Moet niks uit selfsug of eersug doen nie. Ag eerder in nederigheid die ander hoër as julleself.’

Ons lewe in ’n wêreld wat vir ons sê om onsself te bevorder, ons beeld te bou, raakgesien te word en eerste te wees. Kersfees wys ons ’n God wat die teenoorgestelde gekies het: Hy het laag gekom, ander gedien en hulle beswil bo sy eie gemak gestel. Nederigheid is nie om sleg van jouself te dink nie. Dit is om minder aan jouself en meer aan ander te dink, omdat jy veilig is in God se liefde.

verse.text: Hy het Hom ontledig deur die gestalte van ’n dienskneg aan te neem en aan mense gelyk te word.

en.title: The King in a Manger
story: When Mary and Joseph finally reached Bethlehem, the town was crowded with people who had come for the census. Luke tells us simply that ‘there was no guest room available for them’.

So the Son of God was born in a place where animals were kept, probably a stable or the lower room of a house where animals were brought in at night. Mary ‘wrapped Him in cloths and placed Him in a manger’, a feeding trough for animals.

Think about who this baby was. He was the Son of God, the One through whom the stars, oceans and mountains were made. He could have arrived in a palace, surrounded by servants, with trumpets announcing His birth. Instead He came to a poor family, in a borrowed space, with straw for a bed.

Years later, Paul wrote about what Jesus did: ‘Being in very nature God, He did not consider equality with God something to be used to His own advantage; rather, He made Himself nothing by taking the very nature of a servant, being made in human likeness… He humbled Himself.’ That is called humility: choosing to come low out of love.

Why did the King of the universe come this way? So that nobody would ever be too poor, too ordinary or too unimportant to come close to Him. Shepherds could visit Him. Children could hold His hand. You can come to Him tonight.
There was no room for Jesus in Bethlehem. The question Christmas asks each of us is: is there room for Him in my heart, and in my life?

verse.text: She wrapped Him in cloths and placed Him in a manger, because there was no guest room available for them.

lessons: Jesus, the King of everything, humbled Himself and came as a baby.
Jesus came low so that everyone, rich or poor, could come close to Him.
We can make room for Jesus in our hearts and lives.

af.title: Die Koning in ’n Krip
story: Toe Maria en Josef eindelik in Betlehem aankom, was die dorp stampvol mense wat vir die sensus gekom het. Lukas vertel ons eenvoudig dat ‘daar vir hulle geen plek in die gastekamer was nie’.

So is die Seun van God gebore op ’n plek waar diere gehou is, waarskynlik ’n stal of die onderste kamer van ’n huis waar diere snags ingebring is. Maria het Hom ‘in doeke toegedraai en in ’n krip neergelê’, ’n voerbak vir diere.

Dink oor wie hierdie baba was. Hy was die Seun van God, die Een deur wie die sterre, oseane en berge gemaak is. Hy kon in ’n paleis aangekom het, omring deur diensknegte, met trompette wat sy geboorte aankondig. Maar Hy het na ’n arm familie gekom, in ’n geleende plek, met strooi vir ’n bed.

Jare later het Paulus geskryf oor wat Jesus gedoen het: ‘Al was Hy self God, het Hy sy gelykheid aan God nie vir Homself gehou nie, maar Hom ontledig deur die gestalte van ’n dienskneg aan te neem en aan mense gelyk te word… Hy het Homself verneder.’ Dit noem ons nederigheid: om uit liefde te kies om laag te kom.

Hoekom het die Koning van die heelal so gekom? Sodat niemand ooit te arm, te gewoon of te onbelangrik sou wees om naby aan Hom te kom nie. Skaapwagters kon Hom besoek. Kinders kon sy hand vashou. Jy kan vanaand na Hom toe kom.
Daar was geen plek vir Jesus in Betlehem nie. Die vraag wat Kersfees vir elkeen van ons vra, is: is daar plek vir Hom in my hart, en in my lewe?

verse.text: Sy het Hom in doeke toegedraai en in ’n krip neergelê, omdat daar vir hulle geen plek in die gastekamer was nie.

Jesus het laag gekom sodat almal, ryk of arm, naby aan Hom kan kom.
Ons kan plek maak vir Jesus in ons harte en ons lewe.

en.title: Angels in the Night Sky
story: Out in the fields near Bethlehem, some shepherds were watching their sheep in the dark. It was a quiet, ordinary night. Then suddenly, FLASH! An angel appeared, and God’s glory shone all around them! The shepherds were terrified.

‘Don’t be afraid!’ said the angel. ‘I bring you good news of great joy for all people! Today in Bethlehem a Saviour has been born. He is Christ the Lord! You will find the baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.’
Then the whole sky filled with angels, more than you could count, singing: ‘Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth!’
The shepherds ran to Bethlehem and found baby Jesus, just as the angel had said. Then they told everyone they met! God told the good news first to ordinary shepherds, because Jesus came for everyone.

af.title: Engele in die Naghemel
story: In die veld naby Betlehem het ’n paar skaapwagters in die donker na hulle skape gekyk. Dit was ’n stil, gewone nag. Toe skielik, FLITS! ’n Engel het verskyn, en God se heerlikheid het rondom hulle geskyn! Die skaapwagters was doodbang.

‘Moenie bang wees nie!’ het die engel gesê. ‘Ek bring vir julle goeie nuus wat groot vreugde vir almal sal wees! Vandag is in Betlehem vir julle ’n Verlosser gebore. Hy is Christus die Here! Julle sal die baba in doeke toegedraai in ’n krip vind.’
Toe was die hele hemel skielik vol engele, meer as wat jy kan tel, en hulle het gesing: ‘Eer aan God in die hoogste hemel, en vrede op aarde!’

Die skaapwagters het na Betlehem gehardloop en baba Jesus gevind, net soos die engel gesê het. Toe vertel hulle almal wat hulle teëkom! God het die goeie nuus eerste aan gewone skaapwagters vertel, want Jesus het vir almal gekom.

verse.text: Ek bring vir julle goeie nuus wat groot vreugde sal wees vir al die mense.

lessons: Die goeie nuus van Jesus is vir almal.
God se nuus bring groot vreugde.

en.title: Angels in the Night Sky
story: Out in the fields near Bethlehem, some shepherds were watching their sheep in the dark. It was a quiet, ordinary night. Then suddenly, FLASH! An angel appeared, and God’s glory shone all around them! The shepherds were terrified.

‘Don’t be afraid!’ said the angel. ‘I bring you good news of great joy for all people! Today in Bethlehem a Saviour has been born. He is Christ the Lord! You will find the baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.’
Then the whole sky filled with angels, more than you could count, singing: ‘Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth!’
The shepherds ran to Bethlehem and found baby Jesus, just as the angel had said. Then they told everyone they met! God told the good news first to ordinary shepherds, because Jesus came for everyone.

verse.text: I bring you good news that will bring great joy for all the people.

lessons: The good news of Jesus is for everyone.
God’s news brings great joy.
When we meet Jesus, we want to tell others.
questions: What would you do if you saw a sky full of angels?
Who can we tell the good news to?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for the good news of Jesus!
Fill my heart with joy
and help me tell others. Amen.

mission.text: Sing a Christmas song for someone tomorrow.

en.fact: Shepherds were often looked down on in Jesus’ time, yet God sent his good news to them first!
en.deeper: Why do you think God told shepherds first, instead of kings and queens?
en.journal: Write the angels’ song: ‘Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth!’

en.title: Saviour, Messiah, Lord
story: The first people to hear about the birth of the Son of God were not priests, kings or scholars. They were shepherds working the night shift. Shepherds had a poor reputation in that society; their work made them ritually unclean, and some considered them untrustworthy. God’s choice was deliberate. The good news is for everyone, starting with those at the bottom.

The angel’s announcement is packed with meaning: ‘Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. Today in the town of David a Saviour has been born to you; He is the Messiah, the Lord.’

Look at the three titles. Saviour: the One who rescues. People in the Roman empire called Caesar ‘saviour’; the angel announced the real one. Messiah (Christ in Greek): the Anointed One, the promised King from David’s line whom Israel had been waiting for. Lord: in the Greek Old Testament, the word used for God’s own name. One baby, lying in a feeding trough, carried all three titles.
And the sign they would find? ‘A baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.’ The sign of the Saviour of the world was weakness and humility.

Then a great company of heavenly beings appeared, praising God: ‘Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom His favour rests.’ This peace is more than the absence of war. It is peace with God, the restored relationship that sin had broken.

Notice what the shepherds did. They went ‘with haste’ to see. They told everyone what they had been told about the child. And they returned ‘glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen’. Meeting Jesus led to telling and to worship.

Mary, meanwhile, ‘treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart’. There is room for both responses: the excited telling of the shepherds and the quiet reflection of Mary. Both are ways of responding to Jesus.

verse.text: Today in the town of David a Saviour has been born to you; He is the Messiah, the Lord.

God announced the good news first to ordinary, overlooked people.

af.title: Verlosser, Christus, Here
story: Die eerste mense wat van die geboorte van die Seun van God gehoor het, was nie priesters, konings of geleerdes nie. Hulle was skaapwagters wat die nagskof gewerk het. Skaapwagters het ’n swak reputasie in daardie samelewing gehad; hulle werk het hulle rituëel onrein gemaak, en party het hulle as onbetroubaar beskou. God se keuse was doelbewus. Die goeie nuus is vir almal, en dit begin by die wat heel onder is.

Die engel se aankondiging is vol betekenis: ‘Moenie bang wees nie. Ek bring vir julle goeie nuus wat vir die hele volk groot blydskap sal bring. Vandag is daar vir julle in die stad van Dawid ’n Verlosser gebore; Hy is Christus, die Here.’

Kyk na die drie titels. Verlosser: die Een wat red. Mense in die Romeinse ryk het die keiser ‘verlosser’ genoem; die engel het die regte een aangekondig. Christus (Messias in Hebreeus): die Gesalfde, die beloofde Koning uit Dawid se lyn vir wie Israel gewag het. Here: in die Griekse Ou Testament, die woord wat vir God se eie naam gebruik is. Een baba, wat in ’n voerbak gelê het, het al drie titels gedra.
En die teken wat hulle sou kry? ‘’n Baba wat in doeke toegedraai is en in ’n krip lê.’ Die teken van die Verlosser van die wêreld was swakheid en nederigheid.

Toe het ’n groot menigte hemelse wesens verskyn wat God geprys het: ‘Eer aan God in die hoogste hemel, en vrede op aarde vir die mense in wie Hy ’n welbehae het.’ Hierdie vrede is meer as die afwesigheid van oorlog. Dit is vrede met God, die herstelde verhouding wat sonde gebreek het.

Let op wat die skaapwagters gedoen het. Hulle het ‘haastig’ gegaan om te kyk. Hulle het almal vertel wat aan hulle oor die kind gesê is. En hulle het teruggegaan terwyl hulle ‘God verheerlik en geprys het vir alles wat hulle gehoor en gesien het’. Om Jesus te ontmoet het gelei tot vertel en tot aanbidding.

Maria het intussen ‘al hierdie dinge in haar hart bewaar en daaroor nagedink’. Daar is plek vir albei reaksies: die opgewonde vertel van die skaapwagters en die stil nadenke van Maria. Albei is maniere om op Jesus te reageer.

verse.text: Vandag is daar vir julle in die stad van Dawid ’n Verlosser gebore; Hy is Christus, die Here.

lessons: Jesus is die Verlosser, die Christus en die Here: Redder, beloofde Koning en God.
God het die goeie nuus eerste aan gewone mense wat oor die hoof gesien word, aangekondig.
Om Jesus te ontmoet lei tot aanbidding, tot ander vertel, en tot stil nadenke.

Is jy meer soos die skaapwagters (vertel) of soos Maria (nadink)? Hoe kan jy in albei groei?

en.title: Good News for Everyone
story: On the hillsides outside Bethlehem, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks at night. Shepherds were near the bottom of society. Their work made them dirty and kept them away from the temple, and some people didn’t even trust their word in court.

Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and the glory of the Lord shone around them. They were terrified. But the angel said, ‘Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. Today in the town of David a Saviour has been born to you; He is the Messiah, the Lord. This will be a sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger.’
Notice the three titles. Saviour: the One who rescues us. Messiah (or Christ): the promised, chosen King. Lord: God Himself. All three describe one tiny baby lying in a feeding trough!

Then the sky filled with a great company of angels praising God: ‘Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace to those on whom His favour rests.’ Peace with God was exactly what Jesus had come to bring.
God announced the birth of His Son first, not to kings, priests or famous people, but to ordinary shepherds working the night shift. The good news really is for ‘all the people’.

The shepherds didn’t wait. ‘Let’s go to Bethlehem and see!’ They hurried off and found Mary, Joseph and the baby, just as the angel had said. Then they ‘spread the word’ about this child to everyone they met, and went back to their sheep ‘glorifying and praising God’. When we truly meet Jesus, we can’t keep the good news to ourselves.

verse.text: Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people.

af.title: Goeie Nuus vir Almal
story: Op die heuwels buite Betlehem het skaapwagters snags oor hulle troppe wag gehou. Skaapwagters was naby die onderkant van die samelewing. Hulle werk het hulle vuil gemaak en hulle weggehou van die tempel, en party mense het nie eens hulle woord in ’n hof vertrou nie.

Skielik het ’n engel van die Here aan hulle verskyn, en die heerlikheid van die Here het rondom hulle geskyn. Hulle was doodbang. Maar die engel het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie. Ek bring vir julle goeie nuus wat vir die hele volk groot blydskap sal bring. Vandag is daar vir julle in die stad van Dawid ’n Verlosser gebore; Hy is Christus, die Here. En dit is vir julle die teken: julle sal ’n baba kry wat in doeke toegedraai is en in ’n krip lê.’
Let op die drie titels. Verlosser: die Een wat ons red. Christus (of Messias): die beloofde, gekose Koning. Here: God self. Al drie beskryf een klein babatjie wat in ’n voerbak lê!

Toe het die lug vol engele geword wat God geprys het: ‘Eer aan God in die hoogste hemel, en vrede op aarde vir die mense in wie Hy ’n welbehae het.’ Vrede met God was presies wat Jesus gekom het om te bring.

God het die geboorte van sy Seun eerste aangekondig, nie aan konings, priesters of beroemde mense nie, maar aan gewone skaapwagters wat die nagskof gewerk het. Die goeie nuus is regtig vir ‘die hele volk’.

Die skaapwagters het nie gewag nie. ‘Kom ons gaan na Betlehem en kyk!’ Hulle het gou gegaan en vir Maria, Josef en die baba gekry, net soos die engel gesê het. Toe het hulle oral vertel van hierdie kind, aan almal wat hulle teëgekom het, en teruggegaan na hulle skape terwyl hulle ‘God verheerlik en geprys het’. As ons Jesus regtig ontmoet, kan ons die goeie nuus nie vir onsself hou nie.

verse.text: Moenie bang wees nie. Ek bring vir julle goeie nuus wat vir die hele volk groot blydskap sal bring.

Die goeie nuus van Jesus is vir almal, ook vir mense wat ander oor die hoof sien.

en.title: Follow the Star!
story: Far away in the east, some wise men studied the stars. One night they saw a brand-new, extra-bright star. ‘A new king has been born!’ they said. ‘Let’s go and worship him!’

So they packed their camels with treasure and set off on a long adventure, following the star across deserts and mountains. They went to King Herod’s palace in Jerusalem first, asking, ‘Where is the baby who was born to be king?’ (Herod wasn’t happy about another king at all!) The teachers looked in God’s Word and said, ‘Bethlehem!’

The star went ahead of them and stopped right over the house where Jesus was. The wise men were filled with joy! They bowed down and worshipped Jesus, and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.
They searched for Jesus, and God led them all the way to him.

verse.text: You will look for me and find me when you look for me with all your heart.

lessons: God leads people who are searching for him.
Jesus is worth a long journey to find.
We can give Jesus our best gift: our hearts.

af.title: Volg die Ster!
story: Ver in die ooste het ’n paar wyse manne die sterre bestudeer. Een nag sien hulle ’n splinternuwe, ekstra helder ster. ‘’n Nuwe koning is gebore!’ het hulle gesê. ‘Kom ons gaan aanbid Hom!’

Toe laai hulle hul kamele vol skatte en vertrek op ’n lang avontuur, en volg die ster oor woestyne en berge. Eers het hulle na koning Herodes se paleis in Jerusalem gegaan en gevra: ‘Waar is die baba wat gebore is om koning te wees?’ (Herodes was glad nie bly oor nog ’n koning nie!) Die leermeesters het in God se Woord gekyk en gesê: ‘Betlehem!’
Die ster het voor hulle uit gegaan en reg bo die huis waar Jesus was, gaan staan. Die wyse manne was vol vreugde! Hulle het gebuig en Jesus aanbid, en Hom geskenke van goud, wierook en mirre gegee.
Hulle het na Jesus gesoek, en God het hulle die hele pad na Hom toe gelei.

lessons: God lei mense wat na Hom soek.
Jesus is ’n lang reis werd om te vind.
Ons kan Jesus ons beste geskenk gee: ons harte.

en.title: Seekers and Knowers
story: The Magi (often called wise men) were probably astrologer-scholars from Persia or Babylon. They were Gentiles, outsiders to Israel’s faith, yet God used a star to draw them to His Son. Perhaps they knew Jewish Scriptures from the time when the Jews had been exiled in Babylon centuries earlier. Either way, God met them in their world and led them towards Jesus.

They arrived in Jerusalem asking, ‘Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews?’ That question terrified King Herod, a paranoid ruler who had killed members of his own family to protect his throne.

Herod called the chief priests and teachers of the law, and they gave the correct answer immediately, quoting Micah: ‘In Bethlehem in Judea.’ Here is the striking part: they had the right information. They knew the Scriptures. Bethlehem was less than ten kilometres away. And not one of them went to see.

Meanwhile, the foreign seekers travelled hundreds of kilometres, followed the star to the house, ‘were overjoyed’, bowed down and worshipped. They gave gifts fit for a king: gold, frankincense (used in worship) and myrrh (used for burial, a hint of His coming death).

Matthew is showing us two kinds of people: knowers and seekers. The knowers had Bible knowledge but no hunger for Jesus. The seekers had less information but a hungry heart, and they actually came to Him.

This is a real danger for anyone who grows up around church. It’s possible to know a great deal about Jesus, to know the stories, the verses and the right answers, and never actually come to Him and worship. Knowledge is good, but it is meant to lead us to Him.
God promises, ‘You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.’ The question this Christmas isn’t only ‘What do I know about Jesus?’ but ‘Have I come to Him?’

verse.text: You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.

lessons: God draws seekers from every nation to Jesus.
Knowing about Jesus isn’t the same as coming to Him and worshipping Him.
The Magi’s gifts point to Jesus as King, God and Saviour who would die.
questions: Why do you think the chief priests didn’t go to Bethlehem?
Are you more of a ‘knower’ or a ‘seeker’ right now? Why?
What would it look like to seek Jesus with all your heart this Christmas?

prayer: Jesus, I don’t just want to know about you; I want to know you.
I seek you with all my heart in…

af.title: Soekers en Weters
story: Die wyse manne was waarskynlik sterrekundige geleerdes uit Persië of Babel. Hulle was nie-Jode, buitestanders van Israel se geloof, tog het God ’n ster gebruik om hulle na sy Seun te trek. Miskien het hulle die Joodse Skrifte geken uit die tyd toe die Jode eeue vroeër in Babel in ballingskap was. Hoe ook al, God het hulle in hulle wêreld ontmoet en hulle na Jesus gelei.

Hulle het in Jerusalem aangekom en gevra: ‘Waar is die pasgebore koning van die Jode?’ Daardie vraag het koning Herodes doodbang gemaak, ’n agterdogtige heerser wat lede van sy eie familie doodgemaak het om sy troon te beskerm.

Herodes het die hoofpriesters en wetgeleerdes geroep, en hulle het dadelik die regte antwoord gegee, uit Miga aangehaal: ‘In Betlehem in Judea.’ Hier is die opvallende deel: hulle het die regte inligting gehad. Hulle het die Skrif geken. Betlehem was minder as tien kilometer ver. En nie een van hulle het gaan kyk nie.

Intussen het die vreemde soekers honderde kilometers gereis, die ster na die huis gevolg, ‘was baie bly’, gebuig en aanbid. Hulle het geskenke gegee wat by ’n koning pas: goud, wierook (gebruik in aanbidding) en mirre (gebruik vir begrafnis, ’n wenk van sy komende dood).

Matteus wys ons twee soorte mense: weters en soekers. Die weters het Bybelkennis gehad, maar geen honger na Jesus nie. Die soekers het minder inligting gehad, maar ’n honger hart, en hulle het werklik na Hom toe gekom.

Dit is ’n regte gevaar vir enigiemand wat rondom die kerk grootword. Dit is moontlik om baie oor Jesus te weet, die stories, die verse en die regte antwoorde te ken, en nooit werklik na Hom toe te kom en Hom te aanbid nie. Kennis is goed, maar dit is bedoel om ons na Hom te lei.
God belowe: ‘Julle sal My soek en vind as julle My met julle hele hart soek.’ Die vraag hierdie Kersfees is nie net ‘Wat weet ek van Jesus?’ nie, maar ‘Het ek na Hom toe gekom?’

verse.text: Julle sal My soek en vind as julle My met julle hele hart soek.

lessons: God trek soekers uit elke nasie na Jesus.
Om van Jesus te weet is nie dieselfde as om na Hom toe te kom en Hom te aanbid nie.
Die wyse manne se geskenke wys na Jesus as Koning, God en Verlosser wat sou sterf.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het die hoofpriesters nie na Betlehem gegaan nie?

Hoe sou dit lyk om Jesus hierdie Kersfees met jou hele hart te soek?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Vra Jesus: ‘Soek ek U, of weet ek net van U?’ Luister eerlik. Vra dan: ‘Watter geskenk wil U van my hê?’ Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, ek wil nie net van U weet nie; ek wil U ken.
Ek soek U met my hele hart in…
Ek bring vir U my geskenk: …

mission.text: Kies hierdie Kersfees ’n betekenisvolle ‘geskenk’ vir Jesus (tyd, ’n daad van diens, ’n gewoonte) en gee dit.

af.journal: Skryf twee lyste: ‘Dinge wat ek van Jesus weet’ en ‘Maniere waarop ek werklik na Hom toe gekom het’. Wat sien jy raak?

en.title: Follow the Star
story: Far, far away, some wise men saw a bright new star. Twinkle, twinkle!
‘A new King is born! Let’s go and find Him!’
They rode their camels a long, long way, following the star.
The star stopped over the house where Jesus was!
They gave Jesus presents: gold and sweet-smelling gifts. They loved Him!

verse.text: When you look for God, you will find Him.

en.action: Twinkle your fingers like a star, then ride a bumpy camel around the room. Bow down and give Jesus a pretend present!
lessons: When I look for Jesus, I will find Him.
questions: What present would you give Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
I give you my heart. Amen.

af.title: Volg die Ster
story: Ver, ver weg het ’n paar wyse manne ’n helder nuwe ster gesien. Vonkel, vonkel!
‘’n Nuwe Koning is gebore! Kom ons gaan soek Hom!’
Hulle het op hulle kamele ’n lang, lang pad gery en die ster gevolg.
Die ster het bo die huis gaan staan waar Jesus was!
Hulle het vir Jesus geskenke gegee: goud en lekkerruik-geskenke. Hulle was lief vir Hom!

verse.text: As jy na God soek, sal jy Hom vind.

af.action: Laat jou vingers soos ’n ster vonkel, en ry dan op ’n hobbelende kameel om die kamer. Buig en gee vir Jesus ’n kamma-geskenk!
lessons: As ek na Jesus soek, sal ek Hom vind.
questions: Watter geskenk sou jy vir Jesus gee?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
ek gee U my hart. Amen.

en.title: Seekers Find Him
story: Some time after Jesus was born, Magi (wise men who studied the stars) arrived in Jerusalem from the east, probably from the region of Persia or Babylon. ‘Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw His star when it rose and have come to worship Him.’ These were foreigners, not Jews, and yet God had led them to look for His Son.

King Herod was deeply disturbed. He was a jealous, cruel ruler who couldn’t bear the idea of another king. He called the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked where the Messiah would be born. They knew the answer straight away from Micah’s prophecy: ‘In Bethlehem in Judea.’

Notice something strange: the religious experts knew exactly where the Messiah would be born, just ten kilometres away, but not one of them went to look! The foreign seekers travelled hundreds of kilometres, while the people with the right answers stayed at home.
Herod secretly told the Magi to find the child and report back, ‘so that I too may go and worship Him’. That was a lie: Herod wanted to kill Jesus.

The Magi set off, and the star went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. ‘When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.’ They entered the house, bowed down and worshipped Jesus, then opened their treasures: gold (a gift for a king), frankincense (used in worship of God) and myrrh (used when someone died, pointing to Jesus’ death for us).

God warned the Magi in a dream not to return to Herod, so they went home another way. God says, ‘You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.’ Knowing facts about Jesus isn’t enough; the wise men show us that the right response is to seek Him, worship Him and give Him our very best.

verse.text: You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart.

lessons: God leads people who seek Him, from every nation.
Knowing facts about Jesus isn’t enough; we come to Him and worship Him.
The wise men’s gifts show who Jesus is: King, God and Saviour who would die for us.
questions: Why do you think the religious experts didn’t go to find Jesus?
What did each of the three gifts show about Jesus?
What is the best gift you could give Jesus this Christmas?
en.listen: Be still and ask Jesus: ‘What gift would you love from me?’ Listen. It might be your time, your trust, a talent, or a kind act for someone else.
prayer: Jesus, you are the King, and I worship you.
I want to seek you with all my heart.
This Christmas I give you…

mission.text: Make or wrap a small gift for someone in your family, and give it as a way of honouring Jesus.

en.journal: Draw three treasure chests: gold, frankincense and myrrh. Write what each shows about Jesus. Then draw a fourth chest for your own gift to Him.

af.title: Soekers Vind Hom
story: ’n Tyd nadat Jesus gebore is, het wyse manne (wat die sterre bestudeer het) uit die ooste in Jerusalem aangekom, waarskynlik uit die gebied van Persië of Babel. ‘Waar is die pasgebore koning van die Jode? Ons het sy ster sien opkom en het gekom om Hom te aanbid.’ Dit was vreemdelinge, nie Jode nie, en tog het God hulle gelei om na sy Seun te soek.

Koning Herodes was baie ontsteld. Hy was ’n jaloerse, wrede heerser wat nie die gedagte aan ’n ander koning kon verdra nie. Hy het die hoofpriesters en wetgeleerdes geroep en gevra waar die Messias gebore sou word. Hulle het die antwoord dadelik uit Miga se profesie geweet: ‘In Betlehem in Judea.’

Let op iets vreemds: die godsdienstige kenners het presies geweet waar die Messias gebore sou word, net tien kilometer ver, maar nie een van hulle het gaan kyk nie! Die vreemde soekers het honderde kilometers gereis, terwyl die mense met die regte antwoorde tuis gebly het.
Herodes het die wyse manne in die geheim gevra om die kind te gaan soek en terug te kom, ‘sodat ek ook kan gaan en Hom aanbid’. Dit was ’n leuen: Herodes wou Jesus doodmaak.

Die wyse manne het vertrek, en die ster het voor hulle uit gegaan totdat dit bo die plek gaan staan het waar die kind was. ‘Toe hulle die ster sien, was hulle baie bly.’ Hulle het die huis binnegegaan, gebuig en Jesus aanbid, en toe hulle skatte oopgemaak: goud (’n geskenk vir ’n koning), wierook (gebruik in die aanbidding van God) en mirre (gebruik wanneer iemand gesterf het, wat na Jesus se dood vir ons wys).

God het die wyse manne in ’n droom gewaarsku om nie na Herodes terug te gaan nie, toe gaan hulle met ’n ander pad huis toe. God sê: ‘Julle sal My soek en vind as julle My met julle hele hart soek.’ Om feite oor Jesus te weet is nie genoeg nie; die wyse manne wys ons die regte antwoord is om Hom te soek, Hom te aanbid en Hom ons heel beste te gee.

verse.text: Julle sal My soek en vind as julle My met julle hele hart soek.

lessons: God lei mense wat na Hom soek, uit elke nasie.
Om feite oor Jesus te weet is nie genoeg nie; ons kom na Hom toe en aanbid Hom.
Die wyse manne se geskenke wys wie Jesus is: Koning, God en Verlosser wat vir ons sou sterf.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het die godsdienstige kenners nie gegaan om Jesus te soek nie?
Wat het elkeen van die drie geskenke oor Jesus gewys?
Wat is die beste geskenk wat jy hierdie Kersfees vir Jesus kan gee?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra Jesus: ‘Watter geskenk sou U graag van my wil hê?’ Luister. Dit kan jou tyd wees, jou vertroue, ’n talent, of iets gaafs vir iemand anders.
prayer: Jesus, U is die Koning, en ek aanbid U.
Ek wil U met my hele hart soek.
Hierdie Kersfees gee ek vir U…

mission.text: Maak of draai ’n klein geskenkie toe vir iemand in jou familie, en gee dit as ’n manier om Jesus te eer.

af.journal: Teken drie skatkiste: goud, wierook en mirre. Skryf wat elkeen oor Jesus wys. Teken dan ’n vierde kis vir jou eie geskenk aan Hom.

trait.en: God leads people who look for him
trait.af: God lei mense wat na Hom soek

en.title: The Best Present Ever
story: Tomorrow is Christmas! Can you feel the excitement? Presents under the tree, yummy food, family together.
But why do we give presents at Christmas? Because God gave the very first and very best Christmas present: Jesus!

Do you remember Adam and Eve hiding in the garden? Sin (the wrong things we do) puts a wall between us and God. We can’t climb over that wall on our own. So God, who loves us so much, sent Jesus to break down the wall and bring us back to him. That is why the angel said, ‘A Saviour has been born!’ A saviour is a rescuer.
God didn’t send Jesus because we were good enough. He sent him because he loves us. Not just a little, but SO much. The Bible says, ‘God is love.’ Love is what God is like, all the way through.

verse.text: God loved the world so much that he gave his one and only Son.

lessons: Jesus is God’s gift to us.
God sent Jesus because he loves us so much.
Jesus came to rescue us and bring us back to God.
questions: What is the best present you have ever been given?
How is Jesus an even better present?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for the best present ever: Jesus!
Thank you for loving me so much.
I love you too. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, before opening presents, sing ‘Happy Birthday’ to Jesus.

af.title: Die Beste Geskenk Ooit
story: Môre is dit Kersfees! Kan jy die opwinding voel? Geskenke onder die boom, lekker kos, familie bymekaar.
Maar hoekom gee ons geskenke met Kersfees? Omdat God die heel eerste en heel beste Kersgeskenk gegee het: Jesus!

Onthou jy hoe Adam en Eva in die tuin weggekruip het? Sonde (die verkeerde dinge wat ons doen) sit ’n muur tussen ons en God. Ons kan nie self oor daardie muur klim nie. Toe het God, wat ons so liefhet, Jesus gestuur om die muur af te breek en ons terug te bring na Hom toe, sodat ons weer sy kinders kan wees. Dit is hoekom die engel gesê het: ‘’n Verlosser is gebore!’ ’n Verlosser is ’n Redder.

God het Jesus nie gestuur omdat ons goed genoeg was nie. Hy het Hom gestuur omdat Hy ons liefhet. Nie net ’n bietjie nie, maar SO baie. Die Bybel sê: ‘God is liefde.’ Liefde is hoe God is, heeltemal deur en deur.

verse.text: God het die wêreld so liefgehad dat Hy sy enigste Seun gegee het.

lessons: Jesus is God se geskenk aan ons.
God het Jesus gestuur omdat Hy ons so baie liefhet.
Jesus het gekom om ons te red en terug te bring na God toe.
questions: Wat is die beste geskenk wat jy nog ooit gekry het?
Hoe is Jesus ’n selfs beter geskenk?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir die beste geskenk ooit: Jesus!
Dankie dat U my so baie liefhet.
Ek is ook lief vir U. Amen.

mission.text: Sing môre, voor jy geskenke oopmaak, ‘Veels geluk’ vir Jesus.

en.title: You Must Be Born Again
story: It’s Christmas Eve. Tonight we read a conversation that explains why the baby in the manger came.

Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a member of the ruling council, a respected Bible teacher. He came to Jesus at night, perhaps so others wouldn’t see. He began politely: ‘Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God.’

Jesus went straight to the heart of things: ‘Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.’ Nicodemus was confused: ‘How can someone be born when they are old?’ Jesus explained that He didn’t mean a second physical birth. He meant a spiritual one: being ‘born of water and the Spirit’. ‘Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit.’

This is what the Bible calls regeneration, or the new birth. Because of sin, every person is spiritually dead towards God. We can’t fix that by being more religious; Nicodemus was very religious! We need new life from God. When someone repents of their sin and receives Jesus by faith, the Holy Spirit gives them new life. They become a child of God, with eternal life starting now.

Then Jesus said the words that may be the most famous in the Bible: ‘For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.’

This is the meaning of Christmas. God didn’t send Jesus because we were good enough, but because He loves us. He didn’t send Him to condemn, but to save. The gift is offered to ‘whoever believes’, so no one is excluded.
Nicodemus seems to have taken time to process this. Later he defended Jesus before the council, and after the crucifixion he helped bury Jesus’ body. It seems he became a follower.
Tonight, as you think about presents, consider the greatest gift. Have you received it? If you are not sure, talk to God tonight, and talk to a parent tomorrow.

verse.text: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.

lessons: Everyone needs to be born again: spiritual new life from the Holy Spirit.
We receive new birth by repenting and believing in Jesus, not by being religious.
Jesus came not to condemn but to save; the gift is for ‘whoever believes’.
questions: Why do you think Nicodemus, a religious expert, didn’t understand ‘born again’?
In your own words, how does someone become a child of God?
Have you received God’s gift of new life? If you’re not sure, what questions do you have?
en.listen: Set a timer for two minutes. Read John 3:16 with your own name in place of ‘the world’. Ask God: ‘Have I received your gift? What do you want to say to me tonight?’ Write it down.
prayer: Father, thank you that you loved me so much that you gave Jesus.
I believe in Jesus, and I receive your gift of new life.
Thank you that I am born again as your child.

mission.text: Tomorrow, before opening presents, read Luke 2 with your family, or share what John 3:16 means to you.

en.journal: Write your own version of John 3:16 in your own words, as a prayer of thanks.

af.title: Jy Moet Weergebore Word
story: Dis Oukersaand. Vanaand lees ons ’n gesprek wat verduidelik hoekom die baba in die krip gekom het.

Nikodemus was ’n Fariseër, ’n lid van die regerende raad, ’n gerespekteerde Bybelleraar. Hy het snags na Jesus toe gekom, dalk sodat ander hom nie sou sien nie. Hy het beleefd begin: ‘Rabbi, ons weet U is ’n leraar wat van God af gekom het.’

Jesus het reguit na die hart van die saak gegaan: ‘Dit verseker Ek jou: Niemand kan die koninkryk van God sien as hy nie weergebore word nie.’ Nikodemus was verward: ‘Hoe kan ’n mens gebore word as hy oud is?’ Jesus het verduidelik dat Hy nie ’n tweede liggaamlike geboorte bedoel nie. Hy het ’n geestelike een bedoel: om ‘uit water en Gees gebore’ te word. ‘Wat uit die vlees gebore is, is vlees, maar wat uit die Gees gebore is, is gees.’

Dit is wat die Bybel wedergeboorte noem, of die nuwe geboorte. Vanweë sonde is elke mens geestelik dood teenoor God. Ons kan dit nie regmaak deur meer godsdienstig te wees nie; Nikodemus was baie godsdienstig! Ons het nuwe lewe van God nodig. As iemand hom van sy sonde bekeer en Jesus deur geloof aanneem, gee die Heilige Gees vir hulle nuwe lewe. Hulle word ’n kind van God, met die ewige lewe wat nou begin.

Toe het Jesus die woorde gesê wat dalk die bekendste in die Bybel is: ‘God het die wêreld so liefgehad dat Hy sy enigste Seun gegee het, sodat elkeen wat in Hom glo, nie verlore sal gaan nie, maar die ewige lewe sal hê. Want God het sy Seun nie na die wêreld gestuur om die wêreld te veroordeel nie, maar sodat die wêreld deur Hom gered kan word.’

Dit is die betekenis van Kersfees. God het Jesus nie gestuur omdat ons goed genoeg was nie, maar omdat Hy ons liefhet. Hy het Hom nie gestuur om te veroordeel nie, maar om te red. Die geskenk word aangebied aan ‘elkeen wat glo’, so niemand word uitgesluit nie.

Dit lyk of Nikodemus tyd gevat het om dit te verwerk. Later het hy Jesus voor die raad verdedig, en ná die kruisiging het hy gehelp om Jesus se liggaam te begrawe. Dit lyk of hy ’n volgeling geword het.
Vanaand, terwyl jy aan geskenke dink, dink aan die grootste geskenk. Het jy dit ontvang? As jy nie seker is nie, praat vanaand met God, en praat môre met ’n ouer.

verse.text: God het die wêreld so liefgehad dat Hy sy enigste Seun gegee het, sodat elkeen wat in Hom glo, nie verlore sal gaan nie, maar die ewige lewe sal hê.

lessons: Almal moet weergebore word: geestelike nuwe lewe van die Heilige Gees.
Ons ontvang die nuwe geboorte deur ons te bekeer en in Jesus te glo, nie deur godsdienstig te wees nie.
Jesus het nie gekom om te veroordeel nie, maar om te red; die geskenk is vir ‘elkeen wat glo’.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Nikodemus, ’n godsdienstige kenner, nie ‘weergebore’ verstaan nie?
Hoe word iemand, in jou eie woorde, ’n kind van God?
Het jy God se geskenk van nuwe lewe ontvang? As jy nie seker is nie, watter vrae het jy?
af.listen: Stel ’n tydhouer vir twee minute. Lees Johannes 3:16 met jou eie naam in die plek van ‘die wêreld’. Vra God: ‘Het ek u geskenk ontvang? Wat wil U vanaand vir my sê?’ Skryf dit neer.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U my so liefgehad het dat U Jesus gegee het.
Ek glo in Jesus, en ek ontvang u geskenk van nuwe lewe.
Dankie dat ek as u kind weergebore is.

mission.text: Lees môre, voordat julle geskenke oopmaak, Lukas 2 saam met jou familie, of deel wat Johannes 3:16 vir jou beteken.

af.journal: Skryf jou eie weergawe van Johannes 3:16 in jou eie woorde, as ’n dankgebed.

en.title: The Best Present
story: Tomorrow is Christmas! Presents, presents!
Do you know the very best present ever?
It is JESUS! God gave us Jesus!
God loves us so, so much.
Jesus came to bring us close to God forever.

verse.text: God loved the world so much, He gave us Jesus.

en.action: Pretend to unwrap a big present: rip, rip, rip! Open the box and shout: ‘It’s JESUS!’
lessons: Jesus is God’s best present to me.
questions: What is the best present ever? (Jesus!)
prayer: Thank you, God,

af.action: Maak of jy ’n groot geskenk oopmaak: skeur, skeur, skeur! Maak die boks oop en skree: ‘Dis JESUS!’

questions: Wat is die beste geskenk ooit? (Jesus!)
